=== Delete with subtree removes the item and its children and moves the cursor to the next item
--- given
- a
- b‸
  - b1
    - b2
- c
--- when command delete-with-subtree
--- then
- a
- ‸c

=== Delete with subtree from the middle of the line works the same
--- given
- a
- b‸cd
  - b1
- e
--- when command delete-with-subtree
--- then
- a
- ‸e

=== Delete with subtree on the last item moves the cursor to the previous item
--- given
- a
- b‸
  - b1
--- when command delete-with-subtree
--- then
- ‸a

=== Delete with subtree on the last item lands on the folded item that hides the previous one
--- given
- a ⊟
  - a1
- b‸
--- when command delete-with-subtree
--- then
- ‸a ⊟
  - a1

=== Delete with subtree on the only item leaves an empty item in its shape
--- given
* a‸
  - a1
--- when command delete-with-subtree
--- then
* ‸

=== Delete with subtree from a notes line removes the owning item
--- given
- a
- b
  no‸te
- c
--- when command delete-with-subtree
--- then
- a
- ‸c

=== Delete with subtree on the last child moves the cursor to the parent's next sibling
--- given
- p
  - q
  - r‸
- s
--- when command delete-with-subtree
--- then
- p
  - q
- ‸s

=== Delete with subtree renumbers an ordered list
--- given
1. a
2. b‸
3. c
--- when command delete-with-subtree
--- then
1. a
2. ‸c

=== Delete with subtree with whole items selected removes the run
--- given
- a
⟨- b
  - b1
- c⟩
- d
--- when command delete-with-subtree
--- then
- a
- ‸d

=== Delete with subtree with the cursor after the task box lands after the next box
--- given
- [ ] a‸
- [x] b
--- when command delete-with-subtree
--- then
- [x] ‸b

=== Backspace at the content start still refuses to eat into a full item
--- given
- a
- ‸b
--- when key Backspace
--- then consumed
- a
- ‸b
